```{r Attach packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
source("../common/load-neoipcr.R")
load_neoipcr(dev_pkg_path = "../../../neoipcr")
source("../common/helpers.R")
source("../common/logging.R")
suppressMessages(library(tidyverse, warn.conflicts = FALSE, quietly = TRUE))
configure_logging(report = "validation-report")
```

```{r Initialise locale dependent information}
#| include: false

if(!exists("params")) params <- list()

locale <- Sys.getenv("LC_ALL")
localeObj <- parse_locales(locale)[[1]]
invisible(Sys.setlocale(category = "LC_ALL", locale = locale))
invisible(Sys.setLanguage(localeObj$language))
language <- localeObj$language
sR <- get_string_resources(localeObj)

departmentFilter <- params$departmentFilter
support_email_address <- "NeoIPC-Support@charite.de"
```

```{r Check the rule sentences}
#| include: false

# The rules live in neoipcr, the sentences that render their findings in
# this report's string resources, keyed by rule id, and the tables the
# formatter adds labels and fallbacks with in `_mapping.qmd`. The checks below
# hold these to each other and read nothing else, so they run before the
# import: a report tree that does not match the loaded neoipcr fails without
# reading any data. check_validation_rule_texts() in ../common/helpers.R holds
# the string resources to the rules neoipcr defines, in both directions.
rule_ids <- neoipcr::validation_rule_ids()
check_validation_rule_texts(sR, rule_ids)
# The rules whose findings the list labels as warnings: neoipcr's import
# keeps a patient only a warning flags, so such a finding may be correct as
# entered.
warning_rule_ids <- local({
  severities <- neoipcr::validation_rule_severities()
  as.integer(names(severities)[severities == "warning"])
})

# Every placeholder a rule's sentences name must be a field the rule records,
# as `neoipcr::validation_rule_context_fields()` declares them, or a label the
# formatter adds for the rule, as `context_decorations` in `_mapping.qmd`
# names them; any other placeholder would fail inside the interpolation on
# the first finding that reaches the sentence. A decoration's field must be
# one the rule records, its label map must be one `label_maps()` in
# `_mapping.qmd` returns and must name a string for every value it maps (a
# mistyped key in that function reads as nothing), and its placeholder must be
# named by the rule's sentence, or the formatter would look a label up on
# nothing or for nothing.
# That last check reads the English source sentences: it guards the table
# itself, and a translation that words a sentence without the label still
# renders, since an unused value is simply not interpolated.
maps <- label_maps(sR)
source_problems <- yaml::read_yaml(
  "content/_sR.yaml", handlers = string_resource_handlers())$problems
context_fields <- neoipcr::validation_rule_context_fields()
placeholders <- function(text)
  unique(gsub("[{}]", "", unlist(regmatches(text, gregexpr("\\{[^{}]+\\}", text)))))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(context_decorations))) {
  decoration <- context_decorations[i, ]
  if (!decoration$field %in% context_fields[[as.character(decoration$rule_id)]])
    rlang::abort(sprintf(
      "The decoration of validation rule %d reads the field `%s`, which the rule does not record.",
      decoration$rule_id, decoration$field))
  if (!is.list(maps[[decoration$labels]]))
    rlang::abort(sprintf(
      "The decoration of validation rule %d looks its labels up in `%s`, which is not one of the label maps.",
      decoration$rule_id, decoration$labels))
  unlabelled <- names(Filter(
    function(label) !(is.character(label) && length(label) == 1L), maps[[decoration$labels]]))
  if (length(unlabelled) > 0L)
    rlang::abort(sprintf(
      "The label map `%s` carries no label for the value(s) %s.",
      decoration$labels, paste(unlabelled, collapse = ", ")))
  named_by <- placeholders(unlist(
    source_problems[[as.character(decoration$rule_id)]][
      validation_rule_template_keys(decoration$rule_id)]))
  if (!decoration$placeholder %in% named_by)
    rlang::abort(sprintf(
      "The decoration of validation rule %d fills the placeholder `%s`, which none of the rule's sentences names.",
      decoration$rule_id, decoration$placeholder))
}
# A fallback replaces one recorded field by another, so both must be fields
# the rule records.
for (i in seq_len(nrow(context_fallbacks))) {
  fallback <- context_fallbacks[i, ]
  unrecorded <- setdiff(c(fallback$field, fallback$fallback),
                        context_fields[[as.character(fallback$rule_id)]])
  if (length(unrecorded) > 0L)
    rlang::abort(sprintf(
      "The fallback of validation rule %d reads field(s) the rule does not record: %s.",
      fallback$rule_id, paste(unrecorded, collapse = ", ")))
}
for (rule_id in rule_ids) {
  entry <- sR$problems[[as.character(rule_id)]]
  stray <- setdiff(
    placeholders(unlist(entry[validation_rule_template_keys(rule_id)])),
    c(context_fields[[as.character(rule_id)]],
      context_decorations$placeholder[context_decorations$rule_id == rule_id]))
  if (length(stray) > 0L)
    rlang::abort(sprintf(
      "The sentence(s) of validation rule %d name placeholder(s) the rule does not record: %s.",
      rule_id, paste(stray, collapse = ", ")))
}
```

```{r Data Import}
# No warning/message suppression here: configure_logging() (in the first chunk)
# installs a knitr output hook that routes import_dhis2()'s warnings and messages
# into the unified log channel and keeps them out of the rendered body; a
# `warning=FALSE` here would drop them before the hook can log them.
connection_options <- get_connection_options(
  scheme = params$dhis2Scheme,
  hostname = params$dhis2Hostname,
  port = params$dhis2Port,
  path = params$dhis2Path)

# The problem list links each patient record to its Tracker Capture dashboard
# where the report's readers reach DHIS2: dhis2PublicBaseUrl, which a render
# that reads the data over an internal address passes, or else the address the
# data is read from. The address is checked here, before the import, so an
# unusable one is refused without reading any data.
tracker_capture_base <- get_tracker_capture_base(
  params$dhis2PublicBaseUrl, connection_options)

# The import runs without the validation pass: the report is about the records
# that pass would remove, so they have to be kept and validated here — the
# enrolments without an admission form (rule 26) among them, which the
# import's orphan removal otherwise drops. That also includes the patients
# with no enrolment, which rule 1 is about and which only
# `include_unenrolled_patients` keeps in the dataset.
dataset_options <- neoipcr::dhis2_dataset_options(
  department_filter = departmentFilter,
  include_department = "full",
  include_hospital = "full",
  include_country = "full",
  include_world_bank_class = "full",
  include_patient = "full",
  patient_columns = c("id", "sex", "birth_weight", "gestational_age",
                       "delivery_mode", "multiple_birth", "siblings"),
  include_enrollment = "full",
  include_event = "full",
  include_dhis2_ids = c("departments","patients","enrollments","events"),
  include_incomplete = c("enrollments","events"),
  include_test_data = isTRUE(params$includeTestData),
  include_ineligible_patients = TRUE,
  include_unenrolled_patients = TRUE,
  include_invalid_patients = TRUE,
  locale = locale)

data <- with_error_trace(neoipcr::import_dhis2(
  connection_options = connection_options,
  dataset_options = dataset_options))

# The dashboard links name the program the import resolved by its code.
NeoIPC_ProgramId <- data$metadata$programId
if (is.null(NeoIPC_ProgramId))
  rlang::abort("The imported metadata carries no program id; the dashboard links cannot be built.")
```

```{r Filter metadata to in-scope departments}
#| include: false

# departmentFilter narrows which departments the validation runs over.
# When NULL, every department returned by import_dhis2 is in scope.
departments <- data$metadata$departments
if (!rlang::is_null(departmentFilter))
  departments <- departments |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$code %in% departmentFilter)
```

```{r Validate}
#| include: false

# The state of the validation-exception list, which the header states, as
# validation_exception_state() in reports/common/helpers.R derives it. An
# unusable list is skipped rather than failing the render, so one bad list
# cannot keep every department from its report; the header says so and the
# log names the refusal.
exception <- validation_exception_state(
  params$applyValidationExceptions,
  params$validationExceptionFile,
  params$validationExceptionFileUploadedAt,
  function(path) {
    read <- neoipcr::read_validation_exceptions(path)
    list(list = read, keys = neoipcr::resolve_validation_exceptions(data, read))
  })
exception_state <- exception$state
if (identical(exception_state, "unusable"))
  logWarn("The validation exception list was not applied: {exception$refusal}")
exception_uploaded_at <- validation_exception_upload_time(params$validationExceptionFileUploadedAt)
if (length(exception_uploaded_at) == 1L && is.na(exception_uploaded_at))
  logWarn(logger::skip_formatter(sprintf(
    "The upload time of the validation exception list, '%s', is not an ISO 8601 date and time with seconds and a zone, so the header leaves it out.",
    params$validationExceptionFileUploadedAt)))

# An empty `rules` value (NULL, or `[]` from the command line) means every
# rule; a repeated id is applied once, so the header counts it once. An id
# that is not a whole number is refused here rather than truncated to one.
requested_rules <- unique(unlist(params$rules))
if (length(requested_rules) == 0L) {
  rules <- rule_ids
} else {
  if (!is.numeric(requested_rules) ||
      !all(is.finite(requested_rules) & requested_rules == round(requested_rules)))
    rlang::abort(sprintf(
      "`rules` must name validation rules by their whole-number ids, not %s.",
      paste(requested_rules, collapse = ", ")))
  rules <- as.integer(requested_rules)
}
problems <- neoipcr::validate(data, rules = rules, exceptions = exception$keys)

# A rule the package could not run, for want of a column the dataset does not
# hold, flags nothing and would read as clean. This import asks for every
# tier, so such a skip means the dataset is not what the report expects, and
# the render fails rather than presenting the result as complete.
rules_skipped <- attr(problems, "rules_skipped")
if (length(rules_skipped) > 0L)
  rlang::abort(sprintf(
    "Validation rule(s) %s could not be applied to the imported dataset; see the log for the column each is missing.",
    paste(rules_skipped, collapse = ", ")))

# What the list exempted, counted in records per rule for the header, and,
# for an administrator who asked, how each of its records for these
# departments fared. Both are computed from validate()'s result as it
# returned it: a reshaped copy keeps the run's attributes, so
# validation_summary() would accept it but count its rows against every
# exemption of the run. The usage is that of the whole list validate() was
# given, since whether a record matches does not depend on the rules
# applied; a matched record of a rule the render did not run exempts nothing
# for want of a run, and the appendix leaves it out.
exception_summary <- if (exception_state == "applied")
  neoipcr::validation_summary(problems)
exception_usage <- if (exception_state == "applied" &&
                       isTRUE(params$includeUnusedValidationExceptions))
  neoipcr::validation_exception_usage(data, exception$list, problems)
exception_overview <- validation_exception_overview(
  exception_state, exception_uploaded_at, exception_summary, sR)
records_exempted <- validation_exceptions_exempted(exception_summary)

# The header says which rules produced this report, so a document rendered
# with a subset cannot be read as a clean bill on the rules it skipped.
rules_not_applied <- setdiff(rule_ids, rules)
rules_applied_text <- if (length(rules_not_applied) == 0L) {
  interpolate_translation(sR$rules_applied_all, count = length(rule_ids))
} else {
  interpolate_translation(
    sR$rules_applied_subset,
    applied     = length(rules),
    total       = length(rule_ids),
    not_applied = paste(
      sprintf(
        "%d (%s)",
        rules_not_applied,
        vapply(
          as.character(rules_not_applied),
          # A summary is a translated string handed to the header's
          # template: escaped so it cannot become markup, and set with the
          # same typography as the sentence around it.
          \(id) escape_markdown_translation(sR$problems[[id]]$summary),
          character(1))),
      collapse = "; "))
}
rules_applied_text <- as.character(rules_applied_text)
```
